entries.name: HashCRBM
entries.definition: A conditional RBM training and prediction method that uses spectral hashing of inputs to retrieve distinct training-output configurations and normalizes the conditional model only over that input-dependent support.
entries.identity_notes: This is the HashCRBM method of Mnih, Larochelle and Hinton. It combines a fixed learned input hash with restricted-support conditional energy modeling; neither a generic conditional RBM nor spectral hashing alone defines the method. Retrieval supplies possible output configurations, while learned free energies determine their conditional weights. It is not ordinary k-nearest-neighbor voting or a categorical feature hashing layer. The source allows analogous restricted-support learning for other computable energy models; this record describes its named conditional-RBM construction. limitations: Exact normalization and gradients refer to the deliberately restricted conditional model, not the original full-output-space CRBM. Outputs outside V(u) have zero joint probability, and a joint-mode predictor cannot return them.

Coordinate-wise marginal decisions can lie outside the joint support; this is a loss-dependent prediction decision, not positive model probability for the assembled vector or evidence of factorized output variables.

The retrieved set must be nonempty. The displayed formula supplies no distribution for an empty test-time set; any fallback needs an explicit additional convention. Finite training likelihood also requires the observed target in the support, as occurs when its own stored input is retrieved.

Repeated output configurations across buckets must be deduplicated. Counting occurrences instead changes the base weighting and therefore the distribution and gradients. The n+1 lookup count does not bound the number of retrieved outputs or make their scoring cost constant.

The input code uses a rectangular spectral-hashing approximation; retrieval can omit useful outputs, and coverage assumptions suit limited output variability. A larger Hamming ball is a separate cost/coverage choice. No universal prediction quality, convergence or author-code behavior is certified.

claims.statement: From paired training examples (u,v), learn spectral binary codes for the inputs u and store their associated output vectors v under the code keys. For a query input, the paper retrieves its code bucket and every bucket at Hamming distance one: n+1 bucket accesses for an n-bit code. Union the returned output configurations and remove duplicates to obtain V(u). For nonempty V(u), define p(v|u)=1[v in V(u)] exp(-F(v,u))/sum_(z in V(u)) exp(-F(z,u)), where F is the conditional RBM free energy after summing its hidden units. Fit the conditional energy parameters by exact gradients of this restricted-model negative log likelihood; for a training target in V(u), the gradient is grad F(v,u) minus the restricted-model expectation of grad F(z,u). The hash map and support are fixed during this differentiation. Joint-mode prediction selects the lowest-free-energy retrieved configuration. Alternatively, compute each output-bit marginal by summing the restricted probabilities and choose its mode, which minimizes additive bit-error risk and can produce a vector outside V(u).

entries.name: CD-PercLoss
entries.definition: A conditional RBM training algorithm that contrasts the observed output free energy with that of a prediction selected by input-initialized stochastic search, treating the selected prediction as fixed during differentiation.
entries.identity_notes: This is the CD-PercLoss algorithm defined by Mnih, Larochelle and Hinton as a practical approximation to generalized perceptron-loss training. Unlike standard data-started contrastive divergence, its search begins from the conditioning input and chooses the best free-energy state among its search steps. The training algorithm, the generalized perceptron objective and the conditional RBM architecture are distinct identities. The name does not identify the AIO single-layer linear Perceptron architecture. The paper also allows extension to other models with computable energy or free energy and Gibbs sampling; this record states its conditional-RBM procedure. limitations: Finite search does not certify the global conditional mode. Its approximate free-energy difference can be negative, and its update can be zero when the searched prediction equals the observed target even though another output has lower free energy.

Holding the prediction fixed is an explicit surrogate-update convention. It does not differentiate the sampling/selection process or produce the exact conditional log-likelihood gradient, and it does not guarantee calibrated conditional probabilities.

The selected candidate is the lowest-free-energy state among k generated configurations, not necessarily the last chain state. Search initialization uses the conditioning input rather than the observed target; substituting ordinary data-started CD changes the procedure.

Mean visible initialization and mean-field test updates are deterministic probability-valued computations, distinct from binary equilibrium samples or exact MAP inference. Tie-breaking and any final hard-decision convention need to be specified by an implementation; this record does not infer undocumented author-code behavior.

The displayed loss has no explicit margin. The paper proposes margin-based extensions as future work; those are not silently part of CD-PercLoss. Results for the inspected denoising settings do not establish universal suitability, global convergence or equivalence to the linear perceptron.

claims.statement: For training pair (u,v), initialize each visible value from the logistic input-to-visible prediction sigmoid(b_v+W_uv^T u) when those connections exist; without them, draw independent Bernoulli(0.5) visible values. Holding u fixed, perform k Gibbs updates and retain the k resulting visible configurations. Choose a configuration v_hat with the lowest conditional free energy among those candidates. Update model parameters using the derivative of F(v,u)-F(v_hat,u) with v_hat held constant, contrasting the observed and searched free-energy derivatives. This replaces the generally intractable global minimum in the generalized perceptron loss by a finite stochastic search. The source uses k mean-field updates instead of sampled Gibbs updates for test-time predictions. No partition function enters the frozen-prediction free-energy-difference gradient.

entries.name: Spectral hashing
entries.definition: An unsupervised binary-code learning algorithm that approximates a spectral similarity-preservation objective using a PCA-aligned rectangular data model and zero-thresholded single-coordinate analytic modes.
entries.identity_notes: This is the original Weiss–Torralba–Fergus spectral hashing algorithm. It differs from neural semantic hashing, random-projection locality-sensitive hashing, Laplacian Eigenmaps and the later multidimensional spectral hashing formulation. limitations: The uniform rectangular model is an approximation to the data distribution. The resulting code is not the exact optimum of the discrete balanced-partition problem or necessarily the thresholded eigenvectors of the finite empirical affinity graph.

Equation (2) prints Y^T Y=I while retaining unscaled plus/minus-one entries. Equation (1) instead implies Y^T Y=nI for n observations; an identity normalization requires rescaled real-valued relaxed coordinates. The record preserves this distinction rather than copying the incompatible constraints.

Equation (4) gives the interval width but omits the origin shift unless its x already denotes a shifted coordinate. The mechanism states that shift explicitly. Degenerate axes, zero-threshold ties and points outside fitted intervals require explicit numerical conventions.

Continuous orthogonality does not guarantee empirical balance, decorrelation or independence after thresholding. Excluding outer-product modes avoids one explicit source of deterministic redundancy but does not ensure independent bits; even first and third thresholded modes on one uniform axis are correlated.

The number of bits need not be smaller than the input dimension. Compact storage and approximate-neighbor retrieval are not a guarantee of dimension reduction, exact semantic similarity, universal retrieval accuracy or collision resistance for cryptography. No benchmark ranking, general spectral-convergence theorem or author-code behavior is certified.

claims.statement: The motivation minimizes affinity-weighted squared distances between binary codes, subject to balanced bits and pairwise decorrelation; dropping the binary restriction yields low nonconstant graph-Laplacian modes. The practical algorithm first computes PCA coordinates and fits an interval [a_j,b_j] along each retained nondegenerate axis. Under its uniform-rectangle approximation, enumerate nonconstant single-axis modes with positive integer frequency m, represented in shifted coordinates by cos(m*pi*(x_j-a_j)/(b_j-a_j)). Rank these modes by their analytic eigenvalue order, equivalently increasing squared frequency (m/(b_j-a_j))^2 for a common positive bandwidth, and select the required number of bits. Exclude the constant mode and multidimensional outer-product modes. Threshold each selected function at zero to form binary codes. A new point is projected into the same PCA coordinates and evaluated by these selected functions; hash-table retrieval then compares codes within a chosen Hamming radius.

limitations: The model specifies p(v|u), not the input marginal p(u). Normalizing outputs for one conditioning vector does not supply a shared partition for every other input or a joint model over arbitrary inputs.

Factorial block conditionals do not make the output marginal factorial or its partition, joint mode and coordinate marginals generally tractable. Tiny output spaces or deliberately restricted support are special cases.

A small data-started CD update can reflect poor mixing near the observed output rather than accurate predictions from u alone. Finite CD is not generally the exact conditional likelihood gradient or the gradient of a single fixed objective.

Persistent samples from one conditioning input cannot simply be treated as equilibrium samples for another. The paper’s discussion of persistent-chain impracticality is scoped to its input-specific distributions and training setting; it is not a proof that every conditional persistent method is impossible.

The general family can condition biases or interactions, while the displayed mechanism holds W_vh fixed and changes biases affinely. Gaussian outputs, input-dependent interactions, retrieved-support HashCRBM and perceptron-style training need separate conventions. No historical-priority, universal prediction-quality or author-code claim is asserted.

definition_evidence.locator: Sections 2.1–5, Figure 1 and Equations (8)–(13), PDF pp.2–4; conditional family versus affine-bias specialization in Section 3, p.3; restricted-support and prediction-loss alternatives, Sections 6.1–6.2, pp.5–7

claims.statement: Hold conditioning vector u fixed. In the paper’s binary affine-bias specialization, set a(u)=b_v+(W_uv)^T u and c(u)=b_h+(W_uh)^T u, with visible-by-hidden interaction matrix W_vh. Define E(v,h;u)=-v^T W_vh h-a(u)^T v-c(u)^T h. Marginalizing binary h gives F(v,u)=-a(u)^T v-sum_j log(1+exp(c_j(u)+(W_vh^T v)_j)). Normalize exp(-F(v,u)) over output configurations v to obtain p(v|u), with a partition depending on u. Hidden units given v,u and visible units given h,u have factorial logistic conditionals, but outputs after hidden marginalization can be dependent. Conditional likelihood gradients contrast data-posterior and model expectations at the same u.
